$comment: How USPA's published classification standards map onto this project's categories.
The standards themselves are not transcribed here. They are a machine-readable
table the federation publishes for its own calculator, and it is committed beside
this file under `snapshots/` exactly as it was served, so that a change upstream
arrives as a reviewable diff instead of a silent difference in what a lifter is
told. `standards.sha256` pins the copy this mapping was written against: refreshing
the snapshot without revisiting this document fails the build, which is the point.
What is curated is the translation. The snapshot names its axes in the federation's
own words -- `Cl Raw`, `Full Power`, `80+` -- and this file says what each one means
in terms of the identifiers in `data/sources/categories/uspa.json`. None of it is
derived. A mapping guessed from a string that happens to look like an age range is
a mapping that changes meaning the year the federation renames a division.
Every axis value in the snapshot must appear here, and every mapping here must
appear in the snapshot. Both directions are checked, because a standard nobody can
reach and a mapping that no longer matches anything fail the same way on screen:
a lifter is shown nothing, and nothing looks exactly like a category the federation

standards.$comment: Exported by hand from the federation's published calculator. No machine-fetchable URL has been recorded, so `check:upstream` reports this source as manual and nothing watches it. Recording one here is what puts it under automated drift detection.

$comment:tested: The federation publishes one set of standards and does not split them by drug-tested
status. `null` states that as a fact about the source rather than leaving it to be
inferred from a missing field -- see `ClassificationScope`.
$comment:grades: Rank ascends from the least demanding standard at zero. It is carried rather than
derived from the totals so that a mistranscribed figure is caught as a contradiction
instead of quietly reordering the ladder.
Upstream abbreviates the top grade to `Int'l Elite` to fit a table column. The label
here is the expansion, not a rename.
$comment:lifts: `Full Power` is the three-lift total. The other three are single-lift meets, and
their standards are separate published figures rather than a narrower view of the
total -- which is why the lift is part of a table's scope and is never null.
$comment:weightClasses: Keyed by sex as well as weight, because the two ladders overlap: `52` is a women's
class and a men's class, and they are not the same class.
$comment:divisions: The standards use coarser age bands than the rulebook's divisions, so one band can
cover more than one division. Each band is written out as the divisions it applies
to, rather than matched by comparing age bounds: the bounds agree today, and the
year they stop agreeing a derived mapping would keep producing an answer.
`80+` covers both of the rulebook's divisions above eighty. `Junior 15-19` names the
competition division of the same name exactly, and covers the 16-17 and 18-19
divisions in full; it covers the 13-15 division only at fifteen, so see
`unmappedDivisions` for why partial coverage is left out rather than rounded up.
$comment:unmappedDivisions: Divisions the rulebook defines and this dataset does not cover. Listing them is
required: a division that is neither mapped nor listed here fails the build, so
adding one to the categories document forces a decision instead of quietly
producing a division with no standards.

$comment:quarantine: Rows the federation publishes whose grades do not ascend, listed so that they are
Every one of these is a women's raw 75-79 row whose Master figure sits above its
Elite figure -- in the squat rows, above every other grade in the row. A Master
standard of 120 kg beside an Elite standard of 52.5 kg in the same 52 kg squat is
not a demanding standard, it is a total-shaped number in a squat column.
There is no way to repair it here. Dropping the Master figure alone would publish a
ladder that runs Class I straight to Elite and tell a lifter their next grade is one
they have to skip a rank to reach, so the whole row is withheld and the combination
The list is checked in both directions. A row that fails and is not listed stops the
build, so a new contradiction cannot slip out. A listed row that no longer fails also
stops the build, so the entry is removed the day upstream corrects it rather than
quietly suppressing a row that had become good.
